title: BrushCodex Common Document Envelope v1 (draft)
description: Shared envelope embedded by every BrushCodex document (recipe, palette, inventory, project, technique). Defines stable identity, versioning, attribution, licensing, provenance, links (revision/fork lineage), translations, namespaced extensions, and integrity. Concrete specifications compose `$defs/envelopeCore` via allOf and close the object with `unevaluatedProperties: false`. DRAFT: not frozen; see specs/common/v1/README.md.

envelopeCore.$comment: Reusable, OPEN envelope fragment. Does not close the object, so concrete specs can add their own members via allOf and close with unevaluatedProperties.

$schema.description: Optional pointer to the schema this document claims to conform to.

specVersion.description: Semantic version (SemVer 2.0.0) of the specification the document targets.

id.description: Stable, globally unique document identifier as an absolute URI (e.g. urn:uuid:... or https://...). MUST NOT require a central BrushCodex registry.

revision.description: Opaque revision identifier for this exact document state (UUID, hash, or monotonic token).

updatedAt.description: RFC 3339 last-modified timestamp, when known. SHOULD be >= createdAt.

language.description: Primary content language as a BCP 47 tag, or 'und' if undetermined.

attribution.description: Human-readable credit for the document as a whole: who or what it is based on, and any acknowledgement the author owes. Free text because credit obligations are prose, not structure. It does NOT state or grant a licence (see license), does NOT make anyone an author (see authors), and a consumer MUST preserve it verbatim and MUST NOT parse it into agents. An empty string is invalid — omit the member instead.

links.description: Cross-document links expressing provenance, canonical location, and revision/fork lineage.

provenance.description: Provenance entries describing where the document (or values within it) came from.

extensions.description: Namespaced extension data. Keys MUST be namespaced (reverse-DNS or colon-qualified). Unknown extensions are preserved on round trip when preservation is claimed.

license.description: Content license. At least one of spdxId or name MUST be present. Unknown values are never invented.

spdxId.description: SPDX license identifier (e.g. CC-BY-4.0, Apache-2.0, LicenseRef-... , or the SPDX 'NONE'/'NOASSERTION' tokens).

sourceType.description: Controlled source class. Color-bearing measurements MUST NOT be labelled as physical_measurement unless produced by instrument measurement of a physical sample. digital_approximation is a screen-display approximation of unstated or derived origin (e.g. a third-party colour list) and carries no manufacturer or measurement authority.

reviewStatus.description: Review state under the project's policy. 'approved' does not imply manufacturer endorsement.

transformationVersion.description: Version of the importer/transformer that produced this entry.

method.description: Methodology detail (e.g. measurement geometry, illuminant) for physical measurements.

derivedFrom.description: URIs of documents/values this entry was derived from.

colorValue.description: An sRGB color value. Its meaning (measured, digital swatch, estimate) is declared by the owning item's provenance; never presented as a physical measurement unless provenance says so.

paintRef.description: Canonical paint reference shared by every BrushCodex spec (Recipe, Palette, Inventory, Project). At least one of manufacturer or name MUST be present; nothing else is required, so a literal paint with no catalogue id or color stays valid (the literal fallback for paints with no shared catalogue entry).

ref.description: OPTIONAL document-local anchor other members can point to (e.g. a Recipe step or mixture). Specs without intra-document anchoring simply omit it.

code.description: The manufacturer's printed product code / item number on the bottle (e.g. a Vallejo item number such as 70.950). Distinct from catalogueId (an external stable identifier) and from any internal database id, which MUST NOT appear here.

kind.description: Classifies any component referenced the way paints are (in paints[]/mix[]), bottled or not, by its function in the mixture. Absence means an ordinary pigment paint. A component that does not determine the resulting colour (a medium, thinner, varnish, or additive) is marked here so the color engine skips it in matching, and a renderer SHOULD NOT draw a colour swatch for a non-'paint' kind even when color is present. A household diluent such as water is 'additive'; 'thinner' is for a product sold and identified as a thinner. A colour-bearing component such as a dry pigment stirred into a carrier is 'paint', because it determines the resulting colour. This is function, not purchasability: a consumer MUST NOT infer that an 'additive' is an acquirable product. Ordinary tools are resources, never paintRefs; a consumable material is a paintRef when it joins a mixture at an authored ratio and a resource when used in the process.

chemistry.description: Binder/solvent family — the substitution-safety axis (an enamel MUST NOT be silently substituted for an acrylic layer). These four named values are the binder-family subset of Technique's paintClass vocabulary, plus 'other'; chemistry is distinct from paintClass, which is a broader product-type advisory.

catalogueId.description: OPTIONAL external stable identifier (opaque token or URI). Never required.

resource.description: A tool or non-paint material needed to reproduce a workflow (brush, airbrush, wet palette, sponge, hobby knife, UV lamp, gloves, PVA glue, masking putty, static grass, pigments, IPA, sandpaper, resin, and mediums/varnish where NOT represented as a paint), consumable materials being resources when used in the process. Shared by Recipe.resources, Technique.tools, and Project.toolsUsed. Carries no manufacturer or catalogue identity. A reusable tool MUST NOT be modelled as a paintRef under any usage; a consumable material that joins a mixture at an authored ratio is referenced as a paintRef for that recipe instead (Recipe section 6a carries the worked examples).

kind.description: A reusable tool vs a consumable non-paint material.

optional.description: True when the item is optional rather than required. Absence means required.

specification.description: Optional human-readable specification, e.g. 'Size 2 round', '0.3 mm nozzle', '120-grit'. Never an invented precise value.

quantity.description: Optional human-readable quantity, e.g. 'a few drops', '2 sheets'. Never an invented precise measurement.

documentRef.description: A soft reference to another BrushCodex document by its stable id URI. The referenced document need not be resolvable by the consumer; an unresolved reference is not an error. Shared by Project (recipeRefs/paletteRefs) and Recipe (techniqueRefs).

id.description: The referenced document's stable id URI (its envelope id).

role.description: Coarse, closed grouping/ordering vocabulary shared by Recipe steps and Palette entries. Named specific techniques (pin wash, zenithal, wet blending) use a free-text field (e.g. Recipe step.technique), never this enum, so the vocabulary stays small and stable across the freeze.

target.description: The subject a document is for. Shared by Recipe and Palette so the two cannot drift.

scale.description: Optional scale. Deliberately small: only the two observed measurement systems. Physical height and subject form (e.g. bust) are intentionally NOT collapsed into scale — form belongs to kind/description, and a physical-height system may be added in a future minor version only if evidenced.

system.description: nominal_mm = wargame/heroic nominal size (value like '28' or '32'); ratio = scale-model ratio (value like '1:35').

substrate.description: Physical composition of the subject (drives priming and solvent safety, e.g. a solvent primer will melt bare foam). Distinct from kind (a category) and from the kind value 'material'.

mediaRef.description: A linked media item with its own rights metadata. Shared by Recipe (document media and step media) and Project (results) so the two cannot drift. Media is referenced, never embedded; the author is responsible for the rights of what they link, and a consumer MUST NOT auto-dereference the URL without user intent.

id.description: OPTIONAL document-local anchor, unique within the owning media[] array, so a mediaCitation can point at this item. Not a global identifier and never a database id.

relation.description: OPTIONAL relationship to the document. 'source' = a work the document was derived from (for example a tutorial, class, article, demonstration, or prior record); 'result' = a record of the outcome; 'reference' = material consulted but not derived from. Absent means unstated — never infer one.
relation.$comment: Deliberately three evidenced values. 'source' carries an attribution obligation: it does NOT grant any licence to the linked work.

creator.description: OPTIONAL creator of the linked media, when known — the attribution target for a 'source' relation. Distinct from the document's own authors: deriving a workflow from another work does not make that work's creator an author of the document. MUST NOT be invented.

license.description: OPTIONAL licence of the linked media itself, which is independent of the document's licence. Publicly reachable media is NOT thereby openly licensed; absent means unknown.

mediaCitation.description: A citation of a moment or range in a time-based source the document links (for example the passage of a video, class recording, or demonstration from which a step was derived). Time is carried as seconds so any consumer can seek deterministically without parsing human timecode text.

media.description: Anchor into the owning document's media[].id. OPTIONAL only when the document has exactly one media entry with relation 'source', which the citation then targets.

startSeconds.description: Offset from the start of the media item, in seconds. Fractional values are allowed.

endSeconds.description: OPTIONAL end of the cited range, in seconds. When present it MUST be greater than startSeconds (a semantic rule the schema cannot express). Absent means the citation is a single point, not a zero-length range.

label.description: OPTIONAL citation as the author wrote it (e.g. '1:00-1:35'), preserved verbatim so a round trip through a human-timecode format is loss-free. Renderers MAY show it; they MUST NOT parse it in preference to the seconds members.
